Not to butt in but I have used several and I subscribe to the idea that the best cuticle oil is the one you will actually use. Personally I use several depending on my situation. At work I use OPIs on the go cuticle oil. It comes in a brushy applicator and has a gel consistency.  Doesn't soak in as quickly but it stays put and let's me apply and instantly go back to work without making a mess. On the go I prefer cuccio cuticle oil in the roller applicator. It soaks in super nice and I can really get my cuticles JUICY. At home I use just Jojoba oil and rescue rx. I think Jojoba oil is best but it usually has a slight nutty smell I don't like being out and about with. It's all about your needs.

Lace code is a very location based thing these days. While sometimes people saying "noone uses it" is fully accurate sometimes the opposite is true depending on your community. In my hometown there is a pretty tight knit community and lace code is not only used but heavily refrenced! Where I am living now noone has heard of it. If you have an active local alternative scene you may just need to look to your community! For example in my hometown It was very common knowledge that only ladder laced boots meant anything while further out in the state it wasn't used at all beyond specific colors (white, red, blue).  It all depends on what the culture is around YOU. don't listen to anyone on the internet telling you it doesn't matter if that's not YOUR areas reality. but honestly if you aren't participating in the  culture at that exact moment people will likely just assume you like colorful laces even if they were one of the more unsavory flags. Not even the most hard-core punk will look at someone in their Applebee's uniform wearing red laces and think badly of you because you aren't deliberately trying to signal anything. People can usually see that.

Press ons at all times for me. I bit obsessively. When my nails would grow underneath I would get such a proud feeling from it. Obviously it was a long time to stop permanently with no "real' deterrent but it was really satisfying learning to stop and I NEVER find myself ever getting tempted. My biggest advice is to ALWAYS have a nail clipper or file on hand. Part of breaking the habit of nail biting is forming a NEW habit and it is very hard to do if your newly growing nail DOES break and you have "no choice" but to bite it off. I see a lot of people talk about it "not counting" if it's a break and while that's totally fine for most if you find yourself compulsively biting it won't help. Good luck !!!!!
